goal: Maintain governance-grade reliability for OpenCode agents and validation workflows.
current_phase: v2 host-coexistence shipped on feat/v2-host-coexistence (commit 15c47d8): host-friendly skill allow-all, narrowed shell allowlist with deny-safe ordering, overlay fixes (external_directory ask, experimental.subagent_depth, compaction.keep.tokens), hardened v2 validators, corrected docs. Verified: doctor 24/24, clean 2.0.32 resolved-rule runs, container e2e v2.0.32 43/43 + v1.19.2 regression.
decisions: Pack agents allow all skills (`*`: allow) because a pack cannot enumerate host/plugin skills; the working restriction mechanisms are editing the installed agent file or a v2 `integration.use` policy - global permission rules lose to agent rules, which are appended last (last match wins).

Shell allowlist is limited to content-free diagnostics and test runners; content readers (git diff/log/show, docker logs, kimaki session read) and redirections/`git --output` ask; denies (rm -rf, force-push) are placed LAST so last-match-wins cannot demote them to ask.

Agent frontmatter stays v1-shaped; V2 auto-translates it (conversion optional). Converting the shared agent files to native `permissions` arrays would break v1 hosts (unknown key -> default allow), so native conversion stays deferred behind an installer transform.

V2 conformance rejects only v1-only actions (bash/task/write/patch/doom_loop/lsp); plugin-defined actions (browser/execute) and tolerated v1 keys (list/todowrite) are accepted; unknown actions warn in-place but error in adapter output; nested agents.<id>.permissions are validated.
Container e2e found OpenCode v2 `debug agents` needs 2-3 warm-up calls (empty, then builtins, then full) - host behavior, not a pack bug; use isolated service ports for clean resolution checks.
Use deny-by-default permissions with explicit allowlists.
Nest command patterns under the relevant permission (e.g. bash:) - top-level command keys are inert.
Keep em-advisor/blogger as primary agents (manual switch/@mention) rather than Task-delegatable subagents.
Resolve plugin version/inventory at runtime from the installer marker and package layout, never from the consumer package.json.
Secret-read guard: deny by default (.pem/.key included) with a public-cert allowlist (.crt/.cer/.pub, ca/cert/chain/fullchain .pem); accept the rare Keynote .key false positive.
Disable session sharing (share: disabled) and enable compaction pruning (compaction.prune) for long agent sessions.
Installer writes only $schema/plugin/permission to user configs; opinionated package defaults must never propagate into a project or global opencode.json.
Risk-path review gate is advisory (reports computed risk + PR acknowledgment but never blocks merges); enforcement stays human/Tier 2.

Pre-Commit Review Gate (Pattern 8) runs a concurrent multi-lens panel (requirements/code/security/ux-responsive) on a frozen diff; re-review is scoped to the delta, and the gate is documented for users in site/src/content/docs/review-gate.md.
Loop budgets use one binding per-task currency (<=8 reviewer dispatches, max 2 cycles); gate cycles are a sub-loop and do not multiply the 5-cycle/Pattern 5 budgets.
Lens-reported severity is authoritative - the orchestrator may escalate but never downgrade; security/data-loss findings are panel-bound at any severity.
Pattern 5 (evaluator-optimizer) and Pattern 8 (commit gate) are mutually exclusive on the same artifact.
Tier 1 automated checks fast-fail before Tier 2 lenses; security-surface changes escalate if Tier 1 tooling is unavailable.
Agent-config and schema validators fail closed on malformed permission structures: inline, empty, and duplicate permission blocks, plus duplicate/inline nested skill/task children, are errors.
Shared frontmatter/permission parsing lives in scripts/lib/opencode-schema.js; both validators import it as the single source of truth.
Command frontmatter is limited to description/agent/model/subtask; the non-standard argument-hint field was removed repo-wide.
Keep the CI Go toolchain on 'stable' (reproducibility nit tracked as VAL-2) rather than pinning a version.
OpenCode v2 support requires installer-time target adapters because v1 and v2 config keys are disjoint; the phased plan is tracked in BACKLOG.md.

Unreferenced instruction files are dead weight: OpenCode only loads AGENTS.md plus opencode.json.instructions, so standards live in skills; the instruction dir now holds only shared references (review-gate, ci-cd-hygiene, em-advisor-meetings).
The installer --languages flag filters language skill directories (not instruction files); non-language skills are always kept, and pruned directories are backed up first (fail-closed).

Review-before-commit is enforced in three layers: Pattern 8 staged-diff freeze artifact, a codebase 'never commit' rule, and a versioned pre-commit hook bound to a staged-tree hash via .gate/pass.json. The gate runs before a commit leaves the machine (push/PR); a WIP commit is allowed only to freeze the snapshot.
The pre-commit hook is a local honest-operator guardrail, not a security boundary: the marker is forgeable and --no-verify bypasses it.

Decision grounding (Pattern 9) is triggered by decision structure (T1 one-way door, T2 blast radius, T3 workaround smell, T4 volatility), never by self-reported LLM confidence; a fail-closed parent acceptance rule applies on INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE for T1/T2.

GitHub Pages is not deprecated, but the docs site now runs on Astro Starlight (site/) deployed to Cloudflare Workers Static Assets (DOCS-1 implemented on feat/docs-astro-cloudflare); Cloudflare/Astro docs artifacts stay excluded from the published npm package (DOCS-2 implemented).

The docs site is a self-contained Astro Starlight project in site/ with its own package.json, isolating Astro/wrangler deps from the published pack; it deploys via .github/workflows/deploy-docs.yml (wrangler-action pinned to a commit SHA, environment: production).
GitHub Pages is a convenience move, not a correctness fix - the migration was gated (cycle 1 found 2 highs: unpinned action with a live token + dangling old-Pages refs) rather than rushed.
The docs site is served at https://agnts.elkodr.com/ (Cloudflare Worker custom domain); this origin is the single source for canonical URLs, the sitemap, and README/package links.

OpenCode v1/v2 support is delivered by an installer-time target adapter (scripts/lib/opencode-target.js) plus --target v1|v2|auto; v1 and v2 config keys (plugin/permission vs plugins/permissions) are never co-written, and the manifest records the resolved target so uninstall reverts the right keys.

One plugin file serves both hosts: a v1 named export (AgentsOpencodePlugin) and a v2 default export { id, server, setup } (server is the v1 function, matching the documented dual pattern); v2 setup feature-detects a v1-shaped ctx and no-ops quietly.

Install model is hybrid: the file installer delivers agents/commands/skills/config; a plugin-spec install (plugins: ["agents-opencode"]) delivers skills + hooks/guards only, because a v2 plugin cannot register agents or global config. A coexistence guard skips skill registration when the pack is file-installed.

The global config dir honors XDG_CONFIG_HOME (absolute only) with a legacy-path split-brain warning; verified empirically against opencode 1.19.0 (opencode debug paths resolves config to $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/opencode).
v2 agent/command/config compatibility relies on v2's in-memory translation of v1-shaped files; documented but not yet verified against a live v2 host.

--target auto detects the host via 'opencode --version' (spawnSync with a pinned cwd to avoid repo-local shim resolution, 4s timeout, stderr fallback); major >= 2 selects v2 else v1; AGENTS_OPENCODE_HOST_VERSION overrides detection for tests/CI.

OpenCode v2 support is verified against the published contract, not assumed: the plugin was aligned to the v2.0.30 API (the context hook injects event.system text parts; ctx has no client/app.log so a console fallback is used; ctx.event.subscribe({signal}) is the event API; hook() returns Promise<Registration>), and a disposable Docker sandbox confirmed plugin load, 10 agents, and 27 skills on both opencode 1.19.2 and 2.0.30.

v2 skill descriptors must satisfy Skill.Info exactly (id, name, path, content - 'location' does not exist) and v2-emitted config drops keys v2 marks unsupported; the installer never strips user config for keys it does not manage (a value-equality strip was removed as a data-loss risk).

The v2 secret-read guard stays fail-open by design but emits rate-limited telemetry when a read event has no resolvable path, so a payload-shape mismatch cannot silently disable it; a live-model v2 run is the exit gate before v2 is declared fully supported.
open_risks: v2 `--auto` auto-approves asks, so `external_directory: ask` and the redirect/`--output` guards are soft in auto mode (documented); enforce with deny + explicit allows there.
Test-runner auto-approve executes repo code by design; path-arg forms (pytest /tmp/x.py, npm test --prefix) match the allow patterns.
`kimaki buttons *` auto-approve can be abused for button spam / social engineering (low, accepted per user request).
v2 `debug agents` needs 2-3 warm-up calls on a fresh service; a cold read returns [] or builtins-only.
Scenario-level behavioral eval coverage is still limited.
Agent/instruction line budgets remain tight (orchestrator 197/200, reference 215/250); adding to either requires trimming.
Consumer-visible opencode.json defaults are not yet in the changelog.
Multi-lens panel shares one model - correlated blind spots are irreducible until per-lens model choice is available.
evals/harness/run-evals.js still uses a hand-rolled permission parser (VAL-4) that can drift from the shared module.

v2 runtime hook behaviour (the guard actually blocking a live read, context injection, event subscription) and --target auto detection remain unexercised because the sandbox has no model/API key; this is the tracked exit gate before declaring v2 fully supported.
v2 host wrinkles: the load log goes to stdout, which OpenCode's background service discards; 'opencode debug agents' returns [] on 2.0.30 (use the workspace API instead).
Host detection runs 'opencode --version' via spawnSync; the Windows cmd.exe CWD-vs-PATH behavior is mitigated by a pinned cwd but was not executed on a live Windows opencode.cmd host.
The v2 secret-read guard is best-effort: if a beta v2 host does not expose the tool hook, the plugin warns but the guard is absent.
The pre-commit hook cannot distinguish skip-eligible docs/comment commits from risky ones - it blocks unconditionally, so documentation-only commits need an explicit SKIP_GATE=1 or a marker.
Hardening a new mechanism can legitimately exceed the <=8-dispatch gate budget; the gate on the gate itself ran 5+ cycles.
The pre-commit hook's untrusted-content and read/grep scope rules are instruction-level, not runtime-enforced (the plugin guards only read, not grep).
